title: Casper and the Parish
premise: Astrid Galloway, a concierge at the decaying Casper Hotel, is the unofficial keeper of the parish's secrets—until a guest checks in carrying the diary of Marianne Quill, a woman who vanished eleven years ago. The diary's final entries are dated after her disappearance, and they name the hotel itself. As Astrid follows the diary through the parish's buried history of land deals and quiet betrayals, she realizes the town protected someone by declaring Marianne dead, and that the anniversary dinner will force the truth into the open. In the end Astrid exposes that Marianne faked her death to escape an abusive husband who now runs the parish—and chooses to let the woman go free while burning the page that could have destroyed her.
about_author: Lena Vane spent a decade working night desks in small coastal hotels, where she learned that every register book holds a second story. She writes mysteries about the people who watch, remember, and are never asked what they saw.

chapters.title: The Register Book
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During a rain-soaked October week at the Casper Hotel, a nervous guest named Corwin checks in with a leather diary he claims belonged to his late aunt, Marianne Quill, who vanished eleven years ago. Astrid notices his hands shake when he asks about the parish's anniversary dinner. Emotional beat: unease disguised as routine hospitality.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cleaning Corwin's room, she glimpses the diary open on the bed and sees dates written after Marianne's disappearance. When she confronts him gently, he admits he believes his aunt may still be alive—and that the last entry names the Casper Hotel. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of a door opening that was sealed shut.

chapters.title: What the Parish Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She canvasses old regulars—the butcher, the retired postmistress—who repeat the official story: Marianne drowned, case closed, don't stir it up. Their rehearsed unanimity tells Astrid more than any alibi. A threatening note appears under her apartment door. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only one asking questions.

chapters.title: The Husband Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She researches Aldous Quill, Marianne's widower, now the parish council chairman hosting the anniversary dinner. His grief is polished, public, and slightly too perfect. Astrid finds an old police report hinting at domestic calls to the house before the disappearance. Emotional beat: cold recognition of how power curates its own innocence.

chapters.title: Corwin's Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Digging into Corwin, she discovers he isn't Marianne's nephew—he's her son, given up as a child, searching for the mother whose handwriting he barely knew. His deception fractures their fragile alliance. Emotional beat: betrayal that is also heartbreak; two invisible people failing each other.

chapters.title: The Room Behind the Linen Closet
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following a detail from the diary—a window facing the water tower—Astrid finds a sealed service room in the hotel's oldest wing with a cot, canned food, and a woman's hairbrush. Someone lived here, recently. The hotel's ancient owner, Mrs. Voss, catches her and says only: 'Some guests pay to be unregistered.' Emotional beat: vertigo—the mystery was inside her own walls.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the eve of the dinner, Aldous confronts Astrid in the lobby, offering her money and implying her own precarious immigration status makes discretion wise. She understands the price of survival has always been silence—and that he knows exactly how much hers costs. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Woman in Room 9
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid stages a midnight meeting and finally faces Marianne herself, alive, weathered, hiding in the hotel for weeks waiting for the courage to leave forever. Marianne confesses she staged her drowning to escape Aldous, and the diary was her son's inheritance—one she never meant him to find unfinished. Emotional beat: compassion colliding with the law.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Aldous raises his glass to his lost wife before the whole parish. Astrid stands and reads aloud not the confession, but a single diary line describing his violence—then reveals the sealed room's evidence. The parish's polite facade cracks as guests realize what they've toasted for eleven years. Emotional beat: public reckoning; the climax of voice against power.

chapters.title: Unregistered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Weeks later, Aldous is under investigation, Marianne has slipped away to a new life with Corwin's address in her pocket, and Astrid quietly burns the diary's most damning pages. Checking in a new guest, she realizes she is no longer invisible to herself. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—justice imperfect, belonging earned.
